beats: Your tuition slip is worth real money at tax time. The question is: whose money?
Your school's T2202 shows your eligible tuition. Federally, it's a fourteen percent credit, if you paid that school more than a hundred dollars.
Eight thousand in tuition? That's a credit worth one thousand, one hundred and twenty dollars.
But it's yours first: it must bring your own tax to zero. Earned twelve thousand at a summer job? You already owe nothing federally.
So you can pass up to five thousand of this year's tuition to one parent, grandparent or spouse. That's seven hundred off their tax, if they owe tax.
The other three thousand stays with you, with no expiry. Worth four hundred and twenty dollars, but only on your own future return.
And the education and textbook amounts? Federally, they ended after twenty sixteen. Tuition is what's left.
Next: Manitoba's tax brackets on a real paycheque. Follow so you don't miss it.
